transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um… I think what finally made me come in is that I’m having a hard time staying with things I really need to follow. Like at work, I’ll sit down to start an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I fully intend to track what’s being said… and then a few minutes later I realize my mind has wandered completely.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I’ll be staring at the same numbers and rereading them over and over, or I’ll realize I missed the main point of the discussion. And these are things I should be able to follow in my role. I mean, I manage health services, so metrics are kind of the whole job, but my brain just… slips off somewhere else before I notice.
Has this kind of difficulty with focusing or keeping your attention happened in other situations outside of work, like when you're reading, watching something, or talking with friends or family?

Yeah, I mean… the work part is the clearest example, because that’s where it’s really causing problems. Like I’ll sit down to do an EPIC quality report, and I really do mean to focus on it, or I’ll be in one of those clinic metrics meetings where everyone’s talking through numbers and trends, and within a few minutes I’m just… gone mentally.

Then I catch myself rereading the same line of numbers, or I realize people have moved on and I missed the whole point. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to tune out. I know it matters. It’s just like my attention slips away before I even notice.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed this kind of difficulty staying focused in other parts of your life, like when you’re reading, watching TV, or talking with friends and family?

Yeah, I mean… I know you’re asking about outside of work, and I’m trying to think of a clean example, but honestly the thing that made me come in is still mostly those work situations. Like I’ll start an EPIC quality report or sit in a clinic metrics meeting really meaning to follow along, and then within a few minutes my mind has drifted so far that I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed the whole point.

It’s not that I don’t care—if anything I care too much, because then I get embarrassed and start trying to piece together what I missed. But I guess that same kind of “slipping off” can happen when something takes sustained attention. The work examples are just the ones where it’s most obvious and frustrating.
Have you noticed this same kind of difficulty staying focused during everyday activities outside of work, like reading a book, watching TV, or having a conversation with someone?

Yeah… I guess the honest answer is that the work examples are the ones I keep coming back to, because that’s where it feels like it has consequences. Like I can sit down with an EPIC quality report—fully intending to just get through it—or be in a clinic metrics meeting trying to follow the numbers, and within a few minutes my mind has gone somewhere else entirely.

And then I’m rereading the same figures, like, “Wait, what did I just look at?” or I realize the discussion moved on and I missed the point. It’s that same kind of sustained attention thing. Outside of work, I’m sure it happens too, but the clearest, most embarrassing examples are those reports and meetings.

Can you think of any time outside of work—like when you're reading a book, watching TV, or having a conversation—where you've noticed the same kind of attention slipping, even if it wasn’t as impactful as the situations at work?

Yeah… I’m trying to think of a non-work example, and I know that’s what you’re asking. It’s just that what really pushed me to come in is still the work version of it.

Like, I’ll sit down to do an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I honestly have every intention of following it. I’m not bored on purpose or blowing it off. But within a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far that I’m rereading the same numbers like they’re brand new, or I realize I missed the whole point of what everyone was just discussing.

And then I feel embarrassed, because I’m trying to catch back up without making it obvious. So… outside of work, I’m sure there are smaller versions, but the clearest one I can really point to is that sustained-attention thing with reports and meetings.

Can you think of any specific times outside of work—like when you’re reading, watching TV, or talking with someone—where you’ve noticed the same kind of attention slipping, even if it wasn’t a big deal at the time?

Yeah, I know you’re asking for something like reading or TV, and I’m sort of circling around it… I think the reason I keep going back to work is because that’s where it’s undeniable.

Like, what finally pushed me to come in was I’d start an EPIC quality report, or I’d sit down in a clinic metrics meeting, and I really did mean to track what was happening. I’d have my coffee, my notes, everything, and then a few minutes later it’s like my brain has wandered off without asking me. I’m staring at the same numbers again, or I suddenly realize the conversation moved on and I missed the whole point.

Outside of work, I’m sure it happens in smaller ways, but those are the examples that feel the clearest to me.
Can you think of a specific time when you were reading a book, watching TV, or talking with someone where your attention drifted away in the same way it does during work meetings or reports?

I know you’re asking for reading or TV specifically, and I’m trying to land on one, but honestly the thing I can really describe clearly is still the work version.

Like, I’ll start an EPIC quality report thinking, “Okay, I’m going to focus and get through this,” or I’ll sit in a clinic metrics meeting and really intend to follow the numbers. And then within a few minutes my mind is just… gone. I’ll be looking at the same numbers again like I never saw them, or suddenly realize everyone has moved on and I missed the main point of what was just discussed.

So I’m sure it happens in regular life too, but the specific example I can really put my finger on is that same drifting during reports and meetings.

So a specific non-work moment isn’t coming to me right now, but that pattern—that slipping away even when I’m trying—is exactly what happens in those reports and meetings.
